summary: The note surveys blockchain startups applying the technology beyond cryptocurrency, in supply chain, real estate, healthcare and art. It cites a rise in investment and quotes founders and a venture capitalist. It then examines risks including energy use, hype versus reality, legacy-system integration, smart contract security flaws, scalability limits and uncertain regulation, and concludes the outcome could be transformative success or instructive failure.
one_line: Blockchain startups are pushing into supply chain, real estate, healthcare and art, but face environmental, technical, hype and regulatory risks that could undermine their promise.
key_facts: Satoshi Nakamoto introduced Bitcoin in 2009, and its underlying technology, blockchain, is now being applied beyond financial transactions.
A Venture Scanner report on September 15, 2023 showed a sharp increase in investment for blockchain startups focused on non-cryptocurrency applications.
Marcus Whitmore, CEO of ChainSecure, spoke at the TechFrontiers Conference in November 2023, saying blockchain's immutable record-keeping can fortify supply chain integrity.
ChainSecure uses blockchain to create transparent supply chains, reducing fraud and ensuring authenticity from production to consumer.

PropChain is building smart contracts to handle escrows, title checks and mortgage approvals in real estate; cofounder Laura Keller said on October 3, 2023, "We're not just simplifying transactions; we're rebuilding trust in property markets."
Medichain aims to store medical records securely and grant access only through explicit patient consent, addressing breaches and unauthorized access in current electronic medical records systems.
ArtLedger tokenizes artwork to simplify ownership transfer and provenance tracking and to reduce forgeries.
GreenerChain, which emerged in late 2023, aims to develop more energy-efficient consensus algorithms, because proof-of-work blockchains consume immense amounts of energy.
Venture capitalist Samantha Klein said on September 20, 2023, "For every startup that launches with a viable product, there are ten peddling vaporware."
The note compares integrating blockchain into legacy IT systems to open-heart surgery rather than a routine checkup.
A single flaw in a smart contract's code could be exploited and cause colossal damage, so decentralized ledgers are not infallible.
Ethereum-based networks have faced scalability bottlenecks; layer-two scaling and alternative blockchains are possible solutions.
IntrepidLedger, which aims to combine blockchain with financial reporting, faces significant risk from restrictive or patchwork regulation.
